title: L(2,1)-labellings of the regular 4-polytopes
statement: An L(2,1)-labelling gives every vertex a non-negative integer label so that adjacent vertices get labels at least 2 apart and vertices at distance 2 get different labels; its span is the largest label, and lambda(G) is the smallest span. Determine lambda(G) for the graphs of the six regular convex 4-polytopes (the 5-cell K5; the tesseract, 16 vertices; the 16-cell, 8 vertices; the 24-cell, 24 vertices, 8-regular; the 600-cell, 120 vertices, 12-regular; the 120-cell, 600 vertices, 4-regular) and of the two E8 polytopes 3_21 (Gosset, 56 vertices, 27-regular) and 4_21 (the 240 roots of E8, 56-regular), each vertex adjacent to its nearest neighbours. First values (ours): the 5-cell 8 (exact); the tesseract (8-cell) 7 (exact); the 16-cell 10 (exact); the 24-cell 13; the 600-cell 24; the 120-cell 9; the Gosset polytope 3_21 55. The headline cell is the 120-cell: find a certificate with value 8 or less (lambda >= Delta + 1 (Griggs and Yeh): >= 5 for the 120-cell), or prove 9 optimal.
submission: Text file: one label per vertex, in the checker's vertex order (the 120-cell).
score: the span, the largest label (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: 9 for the 120-cell, best found: CP-SAT (one worker, 5 to 60 seconds) on the model of tools/polytope_sets.py, or, for zero forcing and power domination, greedy completion and pruning between rounds of fort cuts

context: L(2,1)-labellings model frequency assignment, where nearby transmitters need different and adjacent ones well-separated channels (Griggs and Yeh 1992, after Roberts); lambda >= Delta + 1, and the Griggs-Yeh conjecture lambda <= Delta^2 is proved for large Delta (Havet, Reed and Sereni). Values are known for paths, cycles, grids and many products, and bounds for hypercubes; for these polytope graphs nothing was found.
references: J. R. Griggs, R. K. Yeh, Labelling graphs with a condition at distance 2, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 5 (1992) 586-595
F. Havet, B. Reed, J.-S. Sereni, L(2,1)-labelling of graphs, Proc. SODA 2008
H. S. M. Coxeter, Regular Polytopes (3rd ed., Dover 1973)
the vertex numbering of checkers/orig_phys.py (polytope_graph), shared by every polytope problem of the Originals

novelty.verdict: new. No L(2,1) result for the 600-cell, the 120-cell, the 24-cell or the E8 polytopes (searched with E8 and Gosset) was found on arXiv, in the journal literature (Crossref) or by web search; the known values for hypercubes and complete graphs cover only the small cells.
closest: General results on L(2,1) (the references) and its values for hypercubes, grids and products; none for these polytopes.
Our polytope problems (polytope-ising, potts3-600, cell600-idcode, cell600-forest, cell120-coil, e8-idcode, e8-resolving): other invariants of the same graphs.

baseline.text: 9 for the 120-cell, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: the certificate in `refs/poly-l21.txt` (best found: CP-SAT (one worker, 5 to 60 seconds) on the model of tools/polytope_sets.py, or, for zero forcing and power domination, greedy completion and pruning between rounds of fort cuts). All cells: the 5-cell 8 (exact); the tesseract (8-cell) 7 (exact); the 16-cell 10 (exact); the 24-cell 13; the 600-cell 24; the 120-cell 9; the Gosset polytope 3_21 55. Bound: 5 (lambda >= Delta + 1 (Griggs and Yeh), for the 120-cell).
